Bench: Surya Kant, Dipankar Datta  ITEM NO.17 COURT NO.5 SECTION II-B  S U P R E M E C O U R T O F I N D I A  RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS  SPECIAL LEAVE PETITION (CRIMINAL)... Diary No(s).46699/2018  (Arising out of impugned final judgment and order dated 05-07-2018  in CRA No. 188/2014 05-07-2018 in CRA No. 151/2014 passed by the  High Court At Calcutta)
 SANJIT SAHA & ANR. Petitioner(s)
 VERSUS  STATE OF WEST BENGAL Respondent(s)
 (IA No. 32343/2019 - CONDONATION OF DELAY IN FILING, IA  No.32344/2019 - CONDONATION OF DELAY IN REFILING/CURING THE  DEFECTS, IA No. 32345/2019 - EXEMPTION FROM FILING C/C OF THE  IMPUGNED JUDGMENT)
This matter was called on for hearing today.
HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE SURYA KANT  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE DIPANKAR DATTA

For Petitioner(s) Mr. Pradeep Kumar Mittal, Adv.
 Mr. Anil Kumar, AOR  Mr. Manu, Adv.
 Mrs. Sudesh Gupta, Adv.
 Mr. Saurabh Kumar, Adv.
 For Respondent(s)
 UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following  O R D E R 1. Delay condoned.
2.
It is stated at the outset that petitioner no.2 (Anil Saha) has passed away.
The instant petition qua him has, thus, become infructuous.
3. As regard to petitioner no.1 (Sanjit Saha), we heave heard learned counsel for the petitioner(s) at a considerable length.

sentences.text:
In view of the statement of the victim (PW-2), duly supported by her parents (PW-1 and PW-3),
coupled with the opinion of the Medical Officer (PW-4) and the medical report (Ext.4), we are satisfied that the the concurrent finding of fact by the Courts below, holding the petitioner and his co-accused guilty of committing the offence under Section 376(2)(g) of the Indian Penal Code,
warrants no interference by this Court.
5.
It may be noticed that the High Court has already taken a lenient view by reducing the sentence from 12 years rigorous imprisonment to 10 years rigorous imprisonment.
6. The special leave petitions are, accordingly, dismissed.
7. All pending applications, if any, stand disposed of.

(ARJUN BISHT) (PREETHI T.C.)
COURT MASTER (SH) COURT MASTER (NSH)
